sentences.text: Since its discovery, Spinosaurus has been considered a contender for the largest theropod dinosaur.
Spinosaurus possessed a narrow snout containing straight, conical teeth without serrations.
A 2022 study estimates that Spinosaurus aegyptiacus could have reached a length of 14 meters and a mass of 7.4 metric tons.
A juvenile Spinosaurus specimen described in 2018 is estimated to have measured 1.78 meters in length.
Spinosaurus replaced Tyrannosaurus as the main antagonist in the 2001 film Jurassic Park III.
Spinosaurus appears in various Jurassic Park video games, including Jurassic World Evolution and its sequels.
Spinosaurus has been featured on postage stamps issued by Angola, The Gambia, and Tanzania.
A 21 mm claw from a juvenile Spinosaurus suggests the animal developed semiaquatic adaptations at birth or a very young age.
The genus Spinosaurus was first described by Ernst Stromer in 1915.
The first remains of Spinosaurus were discovered in Egypt in 1912 and formally described by Ernst Stromer in 1915.
Spinosaurus fossils may have first been discovered in October 1898 when Fernand Foureau found two teeth in southern Algeria.
Spinosaurus is known to have consumed both aquatic and terrestrial prey.
A 2010 isotope analysis suggests Spinosaurus had a semiaquatic lifestyle.
Fossils analyzed in 2018 show Spinosaurus had a keeled tail adapted for swimming.
Experiments suggest Spinosaurus tails produced eight times the forward thrust of terrestrial theropods like Coelophysis and Allosaurus.
Unlike basal spinosaurids with round or crescent-shaped sails, Spinosaurus had rectangular dorsal neural spines similar to sailfish fins.
Researchers argue Spinosaurus used its sail to herd fish like a sailfish and its long tail to stun prey like a thresher shark.
Spinosaurus teeth from the Ifezouane Formation show unique features including deep grooves and an attenuated carina.
Spinosaurus is known to have fed on both aquatic and terrestrial prey.
Fossil evidence suggests Spinosaurus may have preyed on crocodyliforms such as Aegisuchus and Laganosuchus found in the Kem Kem Beds.
The type species of the genus Spinosaurus is Spinosaurus aegyptiacus.
Spinosaurus is the type genus of the family Spinosauridae, the subfamily Spinosaurinae, and the tribe Spinosaurini.
The genus Spinosaurus was named by Ernst Stromer in 1915.
Spinosaurus lived in North Africa during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 100 to 94 million years ago.
The subadult Spinosaurus skeleton was found in the Douria Formation of the Kem Kem Beds in Zrigat, Morocco, dating to the Cenomanian stage of the mid-Cretaceous period.
During the Cretaceous, North Africa was a mangrove-dominated coastal environment with vast tidal flats and waterways.
Spinosauridae dominated the mid-Cretaceous ecosystems of North Africa alongside Abelisauroidea and Carcharodontosauridae.
Russell distinguished S. maroccanus from S. aegyptiacus by a neck vertebra ratio of 1.5 versus 1.1, but later authors dispute this due to specimen variability and destruction of the holotype.
The specimen's body proportions are debated because its hind limbs are disproportionately shorter than in previous reconstructions.
In 2015, Serjoscha Evers and colleagues rejected a neotype proposal for FSAC-KK-11888 due to a lack of locality information, geographical separation from the holotype, and anatomical differences.
The function of Spinosaurus's sail or hump is uncertain, with hypotheses including heat regulation and display.
Spinosaurus's prominent back feature could have made it appear larger than it was to intimidate other animals.
Researchers suggested Spinosaurus used its large tail fin for display rather than swimming, based on comparisons with living animals.
Evidence suggests Spinosaurus was semiaquatic, though the extent of its swimming ability remains strongly contested.
